Ltd. effected a business combination pursuant to the terms of an
asset purchase agreement, as amended (the &#147;Asset Purchase
Agreement&#148;), whereby HSNS, as the legal acquirer, purchased
substantially all the assets and operations of Summus, Ltd. The
transaction was accounted for as a &#147;reverse
acquisition&#148; in which Summus, Ltd. is treated as the
accounting acquirer (see Note&nbsp;14).

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
During 2000, in connection with the negotiations of the Asset
Purchase Agreement with Summus, Ltd., HSNS advanced certain
funds to Summus, Ltd. to assist Summus, Ltd. in funding its
operating expenses. These advances, which were evidenced by a
promissory note in favor of HSNS, totaled $1,435,000 as of
December&nbsp;31, 2000. This balance accrued interest compounded
monthly at 8%, was collateralized by Summus, Ltd.&#146;s
investment in HSNS&#146;s stock and was payable within
60&nbsp;days. Upon the closing of the business combination on
February&nbsp;16, 2001, the entire balance of this note plus
accrued interest was canceled.

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
On June&nbsp;20, 1998, HSNS amended its articles of

and to effect a 200-for-1 stock split, thereby increasing its

5,000,000 authorized shares of preferred stock, par value
$.001&nbsp;per&nbsp;share.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

<P align="left">
<B><I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Preferred stock</I></B>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
On February&nbsp;28, 2000, HSNS issued 2,000 shares of its
Series&nbsp;A Convertible Preferred Stock, par value $.001 per
share (the &#147;Series&nbsp;A Preferred Stock&#148;), at a
price of $1,000 per share. Proceeds, net of issuance costs of
$149,048, were $1,850,952. The holders of the Series&nbsp;A
Preferred Stock are entitled to receive cumulative cash
dividends at a rate of 8% per annum of the initial liquidation
preference of $1,000 per share (the &#147;Liquidation
Preference&#148;). Dividends are cumulative from the date of
issuance and are payable, when, as and if declared by the Board
of Directors on June&nbsp;30 and September&nbsp;30 of each year
commencing on September&nbsp;30, 2000. As of December&nbsp;31,
2000 cumulative dividends accrued were $133,333. The holders of
the Series&nbsp;A Preferred Stock are not entitled to vote on
matters submitted to HSNS&#146;s shareholders for voting.
However, approval of holders of a majority of the Series&nbsp;A
Preferred Stock is required prior to the issuance of a new
series of preferred stock that ranks senior to the Series&nbsp;A
Preferred Stock.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
Each share of the Series&nbsp;A Preferred Stock is convertible
at the option of the holder, at any time after the date of
issuance, into shares of common stock equal to the Liquidation
Preference divided by an initial conversion price of $14.24. The
conversion price is subject to adjustment as defined in
HSNS&#146;s articles of incorporation. Since the Series&nbsp;A
Preferred Stock was convertible at the date of issuance and
since the conversion price was below the fair value of the
common stock at the time of issuance, HSNS recorded a beneficial
conversion feature in the amount of $294,900. The beneficial
conversion feature has been added to the historical net loss for
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2000, for purposes of computing
the net loss applicable to common shareholders.

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
During August 1999, HSNS negotiated, on an individual basis,
with each of the holders of the shares issued in connection with
the Company&#146;s acquisition of the Marketers World assets,
and as a result of such negotiations an aggregate of 5,161,100
shares of HSNS&#146;s common stock issued in connection with the
transaction were surrendered for cancellation. This followed
HSNS&#146;s decision to cease all operations associated with the
MWI business in 1998. Since no value was ascribed to the initial
shares issued in connection with the MWI asset acquisition, no
value was ascribed to the subsequent cancellation. Also during
1999, HSNS canceled 555,000 shares of its common stock, 530,000
of which were originally issued in 1998 and 25,000 issued in
1999. In August 1999, HSNS canceled 300,000 shares issued in
September 1998 in connection with the contemplated acquisitions
of HealthTec, Inc. and National Direct Corporation, transactions
that were not ultimately consummated. An additional 230,000
shares were canceled upon HSNS&#146;s determination not to
pursue certain other acquisitions. In August 1999, HSNS canceled
25,000 shares originally issued to Mr.&nbsp;Richdale and his
spouse in consideration for his assistance in HSNS&#146;s
acquisition of shares of Summus Technologies, Inc.&#146;s stock.

<P align="left">
<B>13.&nbsp;&nbsp;Loss Contingencies</B>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">
<B><I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Settlement with William R.
Dunavant</I></B>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
In January 2000, William&nbsp;R. Dunavant
(&#147;Dunavant&#148;), a former shareholder of Summus
Technologies, Inc. who received 350,000&nbsp;shares of
HSNS&nbsp;common stock and $100,000 in cash in exchange for his
shares of Summus Technologies, Inc. stock, filed a lawsuit
against HSNS. Former management of HSNS had entered into an
agreement with Dunavant which obligated HSNS to register the
350,000&nbsp;shares of HSNS common stock under the Securities
Act of 1933 (the &#147;Securities Act&#148;) within a specified
time period. HSNS&#146;s failure to register such shares
resulted in a lawsuit against HSNS seeking damages
of&nbsp;$13,300,000.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
In June 2000, HSNS entered into a settlement agreement with
Dunavant to resolve the lawsuit. This settlement agreement was
amended on October&nbsp;26, 2000 and then again on
December&nbsp;5, 2000. Under the terms of the settlement
agreement, as amended, HSNS issued to Dunavant
1,700,000&nbsp;shares of its restricted common stock in 2000.
The value of these shares, totaling $1.4&nbsp;million, was based
on a discount applied to the traded value of HSNS&#146;s common
stock on the date of issuance. The number of common shares held
by Dunavant at December&nbsp;31, 2000, totaled 2,050,000.
Additionally, HSNS became obligated to issue 25,000&nbsp;shares
of restricted common stock per month and pay $25,000 in cash per
month to Dunavant until a registration statement on
Form&nbsp;S-1, covering the resale of Dunavant&#146;s shares, is
declared effective by the SEC, which will result in the HSNS
shares owned by Dunavant becoming freely tradable. The loss
contingency accrual as of December&nbsp;31, 2000, represents
management&#146;s best estimate of the monthly obligations
subsequent to December&nbsp;31, 2000 that HSNS would incur under
the terms of the agreement with Dunavant through completion of
the registration process. The estimated value of the monthly
share allotment was determined by applying an appropriate
discount to the traded value of HSNS&#146;s common stock as of
December&nbsp;31, 2000.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">
<B><I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The AIC Litigation</I></B>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
On March&nbsp;30, 2001, Analysts International Corporation
(&#147;AIC&#148;) filed a civil summons and complaint in General
Court of Justice, District Court Division, County of Wake, North
Carolina, against High Speed Net Solutions, Inc. The complaint
alleged that HSNS breached certain contracts with AIC, dated
December&nbsp;9, 1999, February&nbsp;11, 2000, April&nbsp;25,
2000, May&nbsp;9, 2000, and May&nbsp;23, 2000, under which AIC
provided us with computer programming services. AIC has
requested that the court enter judgment in its favor for
$358,426, plus pre-judgment interest from September&nbsp;26,
2000 on certain invoices at the rate of 18% per annum,
post-judgment interest at the rate of 8% per annum, reasonable
costs of AIC and other relief the court deems equitable. HSNS
and AIC are negotiating to resolve the matter. The principal
amount of $358,426 is included in accounts payable at
December&nbsp;31, 2000.

<P align="left">
<B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>HSNS&#151;Summus, Ltd.
Business Combination</I></B>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
On February&nbsp;16, 2001, pursuant to the terms of the Asset
Purchase Agreement, HSNS and Summus, Ltd. effected a business
combination (the &#147;Combination&#148;) whereby HSNS, as the
legal acquirer, purchased substantially all the assets and
operations of Summus, Ltd. This transaction was recorded as a
business combination under APB&nbsp;16 because, among other
reasons, (i)&nbsp;HSNS acquired all the operating assets and
liabilities of Summus, Ltd., (ii)&nbsp;the Company was to carry
on all of the activities of the previously separate and
independent enterprises (i.e., HSNS and Summus, Ltd.), and
(iii)&nbsp;Summus, Ltd. is to be liquidated following its
distribution of the equity securities of HSNS received in the
transaction.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
Prior to the Combination, Summus, Ltd. was a technology company
located in Raleigh, North Carolina that provided contract
engineering, research and development in applications related to
image and video compression and communication, and provided
commercial technology in digital media through various methods,
including generating software development kits for resale,
licensing technology, and developing commercial software
products. Its intellectual property included capabilities in
encoding, manipulating, compressing, managing and distributing
digital content. Its core technology for compression, partially
derived from a field of mathematics known as wavelets, used the
brand name of Dynamic Wavelet<SUP>TM</SUP>. Under this brand,
Summus. Ltd. developed and supplied low-complexity, low
bandwidth wavelet technology for compression applications.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
From HSNS&#146;s perspective, the primary business purpose of
entering into the transaction with Summus, Ltd. was to acquire
Summus, Ltd.&#146;s compression technology. Further, HSNS
perceived the combination of the two companies as offering the
potential to create more growth opportunities for the Company
based on the expected enhanced access to capital resources, plus
it provided the opportunity for HSNS to capitalize on its prior
investment in Summus, Ltd.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
Prior to the closing of the Combination, Summus, Ltd. was the
largest shareholder of HSNS. It owned 8,217,781 shares (33.2%)
of HSNS&#146;s common stock, approximately 27.6% on a fully
diluted basis. Immediately after the closing, Summus,
Ltd.&#146;s ownership interest in the Company increased to
20,593,352 shares (55.5%) of the Company&#146;s common stock on
an as-converted basis, approximately (53.1%) on a fully-diluted
basis. The Asset Purchase Agreement contemplates that Summus,
Ltd. will liquidate following the completion of its distribution
of the Company&#146;s securities received in the transaction to
the shareholders of Summus, Ltd. On March&nbsp;13, 2001, Summus,
Ltd. distributed certain of the shares of the Company&#146;s
common stock received in the transaction to the shareholders of
Summus, Ltd. in accordance with their pro rata interests; the
balance of such shares was distributed in mid-July&nbsp;2001.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
In addition to the items described above, the terms of the Asset
Purchase Agreement provided for HSNS&#146;s assumption of
approximately $2.8&nbsp;million of liabilities of Summus, Ltd.
to third parties. All amounts owed by and between HSNS and
Summus, Ltd. were cancelled upon the closing of the Combination.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
All outstanding HSNS options at the Combination Date were
treated as replacement options since the Combination was
accounted for as a reverse acquisition with Summus, Ltd. as the
accounting acquirer. In accordance with FASB Interpretation
No.&nbsp;44, <I>&#147;Accounting for Certain Transactions
Involving Stock Compensation&#148;</I> (&#147;FIN 44&#148;), the
fair values of the vested and unvested HSNS options of
$4.4&nbsp;million and $2.3&nbsp;million, respectively, were
included as components of the consideration paid in the
transaction. The fair values of these options were determined
using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
Since HSNS was the legal acquirer while Summus, Ltd. was the
accounting acquirer, it was necessary to issue new HSNS stock
options to the existing Summus, Ltd. option holders to reflect
the new capitalization resulting from the asset acquisition. The
number of options issued was determined by comparing the total
consideration received by Summus, Ltd in the transaction to the
outstanding equity of Summus, Ltd. prior to the transaction.
Since Summus, Ltd. was the accounting acquirer, no value was
ascribed to these options.

three-year employment agreement with Dr.&nbsp;Bjorn Jawerth.
Under this employment agreement, in exchange for
Dr.&nbsp;Jawerth&#146;s covenant not to compete with the Company
for a period of 18&nbsp;months from and after the termination of
his employment with the Company, the Company issued options to
Dr.&nbsp;Jawerth to purchase 166,667 shares of common stock at
$0.50 per share and 333,333 shares of common stock at $3.75 per
share. Non-cash compensation expense of $541,688 was recorded
upon the issuance of these options as of February&nbsp;16, 2001,
the closing date of the Combination. The issuance of these
options was in lieu of a $500,000 cash payment provided for in
Dr.&nbsp;Jawerth&#146;s employment agreement.

compensation will be determined under the provisions of APB 25,
pursuant to which the compensation cost will be based on the
difference between the stock option exercise price of $1.50 per
share and the traded value of the HSNS common stock on the date
the options are issued.

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
Purchase accounting was applied to the assets and liabilities of

2001, the date of the Combination. The fair market value of HSNS
was determined by applying a discount to the traded value of the
Company&#146;s shares of unrestricted common stock based upon
the discount associated with private sales of such shares (such
shares being &#147;restricted securities&#148; as defined in
Rule&nbsp;144 under the Securities Act) for cash to third
parties within close proximity to the date of the Combination.
Additionally, since the Company, on a post-Combination basis,
assumed the outstanding stock options of HSNS, the fair value of
these options was included in determining the valuation of HSNS.
The value of the consideration described above totaled
$23.5&nbsp;million. The fair value of the HSNS net liabilities
on the date of the Combination totaled approximately
$4.0&nbsp;million, resulting in goodwill valued at approximately
$27.5&nbsp;million.

a judgment by consent in the amount of the Indebtedness, less
any payments made under the settlement agreement, in the event
the Company defaults on its obligations under the settlement
agreement.

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
On March&nbsp;15, 2001, ENELF, LLC filed a civil lawsuit in the
United States District Court for Eastern District of Texas
alleging patent infringement by Microsoft Corporation, Texas
Instruments, Incorporated Aware, Inc. and Summus, Ltd. ENELF
alleged that MaxxNote, MaxxShow and PhotoID SDK infringed upon
ENELF&#146;s U.S. Patent Number 4,599,567 entitled &#147;Signal
Representation Generator&#148; ENELF sought to enjoin Summus,
Ltd. from making, selling, offering for sale, using, or
importing its wavelet-based video and image processing
technology. In addition, ENELF sought an unspecified amount of
monetary damages. The Company has filed an answer denying
ENELF&#146;s allegations, and seeking a declaratory judgment of
non-infringement, invalidity, and unenforceability. The Company
has recently entered into settlement discussions with ENELF, but
is prepared to provide a vigorous defense to this lawsuit. The
Company has not recorded a loss contingency relating to this
complaint because, in management&#146;s opinion, it is not
probable that a loss contingency exists and an amount cannot be
reasonably estimated.

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
I have audited the accompanying balance sheet of Douglas May
&#38; Co., Inc. as of December&nbsp;31, 1999 and the related
statements of income and retained earnings and cash flows for
the year then ended. These financial statements are the
responsibility of the Company&#146;s management. My
responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial
statements based on my audit.

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
I conducted the audit in accordance with auditing standards
generally accepted in the United States. Those standards require
that I plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance
about whether the financial statements are free of material
misstatement. An audit includes examining, on a test basis,
evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial
statements. An audit also includes assessing the accounting
principles used and significant estimates made by management, as
well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation.
I believe that my audit provides a reasonable basis for my
opinion.

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
In my opinion, the financial statements referred to above
present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position
of Douglas May&nbsp;&#38; Co., Inc. at December&nbsp;31, 1999
and the result of its operations and cash flows for the year
then ended, in conformity with accounting principles generally
accepted in the United States.

<P align="center">
<B>Douglas May &#38; Co., Inc.</B>

<P align="center">
<B>Notes to Financial Statements</B>

<P align="center">
<B>December&nbsp;31, 1999</B>

<P align="left">
<B>1.&nbsp;&nbsp;Business and Organization</B>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
Douglas May &#38;&nbsp;Co., Inc. (&#147;May&#148; or the
&#147;Company&#148;) provides media creation services that
include creative design assistance and commercial content
development, development of audio and video images, as well as
web site design and construction. May was incorporated in 1992
and is headquartered in Dallas Texas.

<P align="left">
<B>2.&nbsp;&nbsp;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</B>

<P align="left">
<B><I>&nbsp; Use of Estimates</I></B>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The preparation of financial statements in conformity with
general accepted accounting principals requires management to
make estimate and assumptions that effect the amounts reported
in the financial statements and accompanying notes. Actual
results could differ from those estimates.

<P align="left">
<B><I>&nbsp; Property and equipment</I></B>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
Property and equipment are stated at cost. Depreciation was
calculated using the straight-line basis over the estimate
useful lives of the assets.

<P align="left">
<B><I>&nbsp; Income Taxes</I></B>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
Income taxes are accounted for using the liability method in
accordance with Statement of Financial Accounting Standards
No.&nbsp;109, <I>Accounting for Income Taxes.</I>

<P align="left">
<B><I>&nbsp; Financial Instruments</I></B>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The carrying amount of cash, accounts receivable and accounts
payable approximates fair value for these financial instruments.
Financial instruments that potentially subject the Company to
concentrations of credit risk consist of cash and accounts
receivable. The Company maintains its cash with financial
institutions and periodically performs evaluations of the credit
standings of those financial institutions. The Company&#146;s
customer base consists of companies operating in the United
States. The Company&#146;s exposure to credit risk with respect
to its trade accounts receivable is limited to the carrying
amount of the receivables. The Company does not require
collateral on these financial instruments.

<P align="left">
<B><I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenue Recognition</I></B>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
Revenue is recognized at the time the services are rendered
based on the terms of the individual contracts.

<P align="left">
<B>3.&nbsp;&nbsp;Leases</B>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The Company leases office space under a noncancelable operating
lease. The lease is for 65&nbsp;months. Total rent expense under
the lease for the 1999 was&nbsp;$33,360.

<P align="left">
<B>The HSNS&nbsp;&#151; Summus, Ltd. Business Combination</B>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
On February&nbsp;16, 2001, pursuant to the terms of an asset
purchase agreement, as amended (the &#147;Asset Purchase
Agreement&#148;) High Speed Net Solutions, Inc.
(&#147;HSNS&#148;) and Summus, Ltd. effected a business
combination (the &#147;Combination&#148;) whereby HSNS, as the
legal acquirer, purchased substantially all the assets and
operations of Summus, Ltd. This transaction was recorded as a
business combination under the guidance of Accounting Principles
Board Opinion No.&nbsp;16, &#147;Business Combinations&#148;
(&#147;APB&nbsp;16&#148;) because, among other reasons,
(i)&nbsp;HSNS acquired all the operating assets and liabilities
of Summus, Ltd., (ii)&nbsp;the Company was to carry on all of
the activities of the previously separate and independent
enterprises (i.e., HSNS and Summus, Ltd.), and
(iii)&nbsp;Summus, Ltd. is to be liquidated following its
distribution of the equity securities of HSNS received in the
transaction.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">
<B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Summus, Ltd. as Accounting
Acquirer</I></B>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The acquisition of the assets and operations of Summus, Ltd. was
accounted for as a &#147;reverse acquisition&#148; in which
Summus, Ltd. is treated as the accounting acquirer; HSNS, the
acquired corporation. Summus, Ltd. was considered the accounting
acquirer in the transaction because Summus, Ltd. received shares
of HSNS&#146;s common stock and other equity securities, to be
distributed to the Summus, Ltd. shareholders, representing the
largest portion (53.1%) of the voting interests in the combined
company (the post-Combination combined company being, for
clarity of reference, referred to as the &#147;Company&#148;).
In reaching this conclusion, the Company determined that there
was not sufficient other evidence to indicate that HSNS should
be deemed the acquirer, taking into consideration that:
(i)&nbsp;the terms of the Asset Purchase Agreement provided for
the Board of Directors of the Company to consist of an equal
number of representatives of both Summus, Ltd. and HSNS, with a
Summus, Ltd. director serving as Chairman of the Board;
(ii)&nbsp;senior management of the Company was to consist of
representatives of each of the companies in roughly equal
numbers; (iii)&nbsp;post-Combination, the Company&#146;s primary
business focus was to be that of Summus, Ltd. at the time of the
closing of the transaction; and (iv)&nbsp;the terms of the
voting trust agreement with Dr.&nbsp;Bjorn Jawerth (entered into
in connection with and upon the closing of the transaction)
provided for the release of the shares of HSNS common stock
subject to the voting arrangements set forth therein in
increments over roughly a one-year period following the closing
of the transaction.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">
<B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Business Purpose of the
Combination</I></B>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
From Summus, Ltd.&#146;s perspective, the primary business
purpose of entering into the transaction with HSNS was to
provide a vehicle for raising capital. Summus, Ltd. was at a
stage in its development where it required additional financing
or needed to combine with another entity in order to finance its
business and realize its other objectives. The business
combination with HSNS became the most logical course of action
to provide financing to Summus, Ltd. and seek to accomplish
other key objectives in view of, among other things, the
following:

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>
<P>

<TABLE width="100%" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<TR>
	<TD width="3%"></TD>
	<TD width="1%"></TD>
	<TD width="96%"></TD>

</FONT></TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
	<TD>&nbsp;</TD>
	<TD>&#149;&nbsp;</TD>
	<TD align="left">
	Summus, Ltd. already had a substantial equity interest in HSNS.
	In fact, the Combination provided both companies the opportunity
	to capitalize on investments they previously made in each other.
	Prior to the Combination, Summus, Ltd. owned approximately 27.6%
	of HSNS and HSNS owned approximately 14% of Summus, Ltd.</TD>

</TR>

</FONT></TD></TR>

<TR valign="top">
	<TD>&nbsp;</TD>
	<TD>&#149;&nbsp;</TD>
	<TD align="left">
	HSNS has had success in raising equity capital through private
	placements or other types of fund-raising, notwithstanding its
	own limited financial resources and unprofitable operations.
	This caused Summus, Ltd.&#146;s management to believe that the
	Company would be able to continue to have success in raising
	capital.</TD>

	liquidity in such stock.</TD>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
In addition, Summus, Ltd. evaluated potential financing
alternatives other than via a business combination with HSNS.
Nearly every institutional investor contacted declined to make
an investment in Summus, Ltd. due to its significant ownership
interest in HSNS, a publicly-held company.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
Based on the foregoing, Summus, Ltd. concluded that the
acquisition of HSNS was the most practical solution to its
financing and growth needs.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">
<B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Valuation of the
Combination</I></B>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The recorded value of the Combination was based on the equity
value of the shares of common stock and other equity securities
HSNS issued to Summus, Ltd. (for distribution to the Summus,
Ltd. shareholders) in the transaction. Since HSNS&#146;s common
stock was traded on the Pink Sheets&#174; on the date the
transaction closed, the fair market value of the shares of such
stock (and other equity securities, on an as-converted basis)
issued in the transaction was more readily determinable than the
fair market value of the shares of common stock of Summus, Ltd.,
a privately-held company, exchanged in consideration for such
shares of HSNS common stock and other equity securities.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The value of the shares of the HSNS common stock and the other
equity securities issued in the transaction was based on the
traded value of such stock on the date of the Combination, less
a discount reflecting: (1)&nbsp;the limited public float of the
common stock and (2)&nbsp;the thinly traded volume of
HSNS&#146;s common stock. The discount applied was similar in
proportion to the discount HSNS realized in connection with cash
sales of its common stock to third parties.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
Another component of the value of the Combination was the value
of the outstanding HSNS stock options. All outstanding HSNS
options on the date of the Combination were treated as
replacement options since the Combination was accounted for as a
reverse acquisition with Summus, Ltd. as the accounting
acquirer. In accordance with FASB Interpretation No.&nbsp;44,
<I>&#147;Accounting for Certain Transaction Involving Stock
Compensation&#148;</I> (&#147;FIN&nbsp;44&#148;), the fair
values of the vested and unvested HSNS options of
$4.4&nbsp;million and $2.3&nbsp;million, respectively, were
included as components of the consideration paid in the
transaction. The fair values of these options were determined
using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
Summus, Ltd., as the accounting acquirer in the Combination,
recorded goodwill in the amount of $27.5&nbsp;million. The
goodwill recorded in connection with the transaction represented
the excess of the purchase price over the fair value of net
assets acquired in accordance with APB 16. The goodwill is not
associated with specific cash flows of the HSNS assets or
operations acquired. Rather, the goodwill is considered to be
enterprise level goodwill associated with the combined value of
the companies resulting from the Combination. The financial
forecast of the Company demonstrates a sufficient amount of cash
flow, on a combined company basis, to fully realize the amount
of recorded goodwill. Additionally, the market capitalization of
the Company of $94.1&nbsp;million at June&nbsp;30, 2001 does not
indicate impairment of the carrying value of the goodwill.
Accordingly, the Company&#146;s management believes that the
amount of goodwill recorded by the Company in connection with
the acquisition of HSNS was determined in accordance with the
guidance of APB 16 and is recoverable.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The acquisition of Douglas May&nbsp;&#38; Co. was made in order

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

<P align="left">
<B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Valuation of the
Transaction</I></B>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The shares of HSNS common stock were valued at $1,376,000. Under
the terms of the share acquisition agreement, the 183,070 shares
of HSNS common stock issued in the transaction were issued in
three allotments. The first allotment corresponded to $500,000
of value. At closing, HSNS issued 50,000 shares of common stock,
such shares being subject to adjustment if the Over-the-Counter
Bulletin Board trading price of the common stock on the first
anniversary of the closing date of the transaction was less than
$10.00 per share. Under such circumstances, HSNS was obligated
to issue additional shares of common stock that, when added to
the 50,000 shares, and multiplied by the per share trading price
on the first anniversary of the closing date, equaled $500,000
in value. The issuance of the 50,000 shares was recorded at the
&#147;guaranteed&#148; amount of $10.00 per share on the date of
issuance, July&nbsp;10, 2000.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The second allotment of shares of common stock (87,498 shares)
issued at closing corresponded to a negotiated value of
$576,000. HSNS committed to file a registration statement with
the SEC to register the resale of these shares. If the shares
were not freely tradable on or before January&nbsp;1, 2001,
Mr.&nbsp;May had the right to cause HSNS to repurchase these
shares from him by making six cash installment payments totaling
$576,000.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
The third allotment of shares of common stock (45,572 shares)
issued at closing corresponded to a negotiated value of
$300,000. HSNS committed to file a registration statement with
the SEC to register the resale of these shares. If the shares
were not freely tradable on or before the expiration of
90&nbsp;days from the closing date, Mr.&nbsp;May had the right
to cause HSNS to repurchase these shares from him by releasing
funds, in the amount of $300,000, which the share acquisition
agreement provided be placed into an escrow account, the funds
being from certain accounts receivable of Douglas May&nbsp;&#38;
Co., Inc. that were collected subsequent to the acquisition
date. In January&nbsp;2001, based on the election of
Mr.&nbsp;May, HSNS repurchased and retired these shares for
$300,000 using the funds from the escrow account. These shares
have been treated as outstanding, prior to the repurchase by
HSNS, for loss per share purposes in accordance with the
guidance set forth in SFAS No.&nbsp;128. All shares issued that
are subject to repurchase by HSNS have been presented on
HSNS&#146;s balance sheet as redeemable stock outside of
stockholder&#146;s equity.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">
<B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Impairment of
Goodwill</I></B>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
Based on the value of the consideration noted above, HSNS
recorded goodwill in the amount of $1,174,437 on the date it
acquired Douglas May&nbsp;&#38; Co.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

</FONT></DIV>

<P align="left">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
During 2000, Douglas May&nbsp;&#38; Co. produced negative cash
flows. In the fourth quarter of 2000, HSNS determined not to
further fund its planned rich media direct business due to
funding constraints. At that time, management determined that
there was no basis upon which to project positive future cash
flows from Douglas May&nbsp;&#38; Co. in the absence of the
anticipated synergies to be derived by incorporating Douglas
May&nbsp;&#38; Co.&#146;s business into HSNS&#146;s rich media
direct business. Thus in accordance with the provisions of SFAS
121, HSNS concluded that the unamortized portion of the goodwill
recorded in connection with the acquisition of Douglas
May&nbsp;&#38; Co. ($1,058,177, net of the previously amortized
amount of $116,260) had become fully impaired and should be
written off. In the fourth quarter of 2000, HSNS recorded an
impairment charge of $3,953,182, which included $1,058,177
related to the goodwill recorded in connection with the
acquisition of Douglas May&nbsp;&#38; Co.

<DIV align="left"><FONT size="1">

Upon the consummation of the Combination, the Company determined
to revise its business plan to focus primarily on Summus,
Ltd.&#146;s business operations immediately prior to the
transaction. The Company chose to focus primarily on Summus,
Ltd.&#146;s business plan because management perceived it had
the potential to create greater
